root_cause.text: Device-managed resources in the ch341 USB SPI driver were tied to the parent USB device (`udev->dev`) instead of the USB interface (`intf->dev`), causing memory leaks and resource lifetime mismatches when the driver is unbound without physical device disconnection.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes all `devm_*` allocations from `&udev->dev` to `&intf->dev` for the SPI controller and driver data buffers (lines 155, 166, 174). USB drivers bind to interfaces, not parent devices, so devres cleanup is triggered on interface unbind. By using the parent device, resources were not released until the USB device was physically disconnected, causing leaks during probe deferral or configuration changes. The CVE description explicitly states this "avoids issues like memory leaks when drivers are unbound without their devices being physically disconnected."

    Signed-off-by: Johannes Thumshirn <jth@kernel.org>

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability is present in the ch341_probe function. At line 151, device-managed resources are allocated using `devm_spi_alloc_master(&udev->dev, ...)`, which ties the SPI controller to the USB device (`udev->dev`) instead of the USB interface (`intf->dev`). This is repeated at lines 161 and 167 where `devm_kzalloc(&udev->dev, ...)` is used for rx_buf and tx_buf allocations. The root cause is that all devm allocations use `&udev->dev` (the parent USB device) rather than `&intf->dev` (the USB interface). When the driver is unbound without physical device disconnection, the device-managed resources tied to udev->dev will not be freed at the correct time, causing memory leaks and resource lifetime mismatches. The disconnect handler (lines 213-219) does not properly clean up device-managed resources because they are tied to the wrong device object. The fix would require changing all `&udev->dev` references to `&intf->dev` in the devm allocation calls.

Author: Johannes Thumshirn <jth@kernel.org>

    spi: add ch341a usb2spi driver
    
    Add a driver for the QiHeng Electronics ch341a USB-to-SPI adapter.
    
    This driver is loosely based on the ch341a module from the flashrom project.
    
    Signed-off-by: Johannes Thumshirn <jth@kernel.org>

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability is present in the ch341_probe function. At line 153, device-managed resources are allocated using `devm_spi_alloc_master(&udev->dev, ...)` where `udev->dev` is the USB device, not the USB interface. This is followed by multiple `devm_kzalloc(&udev->dev, ...)` calls at lines 161 and 169 for rx_buf and tx_buf respectively. The root cause is that all device-managed resources are tied to the parent USB device (`udev->dev`) instead of the USB interface (`intf->dev`). This causes resource lifetime mismatches: when the driver is unbound without physical device disconnection, the devm resources remain tied to the USB device and are not properly cleaned up at unbind time. The correct approach would be to use `devm_spi_alloc_master(&intf->dev, ...)` and `devm_kzalloc(&intf->dev, ...)` to tie the resources to the interface lifecycle. Additionally, there is no explicit cleanup in ch341_disconnect for the devm-allocated resources, relying instead on the USB device's devm cleanup, which doesn't occur on unbind-only scenarios.
